children: The FTSE MIB plunged 1.7% to 51,629 on Monday, amid mounting concerns over global security that reverberated across sectors.
Tech stocks Prysmian (-7.1%) and STMicroelectronics (-6.5%) led the decline after major AI firms called for a slowdown in the boom of capital expenditure on the sector, citing safety concerns.
Expectations of rate hikes by major economies contributed to a surge in sovereign yields, while rising oil prices following the closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline added to the pressure.
MPS fell 2.9% while stating that its buyout offers for BPM and Banca Generali cannot be revoked if Intesa Sanpaolo’s takeover bid goes through.
Defense stocks underperformed as European leaders called for greater investment in Arctic defenses amid pressure from Russia.
Meanwhile, Stellantis dropped 2.8% as it considered selling its factory in Toronto, while Prime Minister Carney turned to the EU following the collapse of trade talks with the US.

title: FTSE MIB Drops Sharply
